complexity.notes: The head-selection logic (root / next1 / next2 setup) repeats the loop's comparison three times; starting from a single dummy node and returning dummy.next would fold all of that into the main loop. The `if list1 is None` guard is also redundant once the `list2 is None` case is handled — the general loop plus splice would cover it, though the early returns are harmless. The final if/else with identical `return root` could be one assignment and one return.
complexity.summary: Iteratively merges the two sorted lists in place by always linking the smaller current node, then splices the remainder of whichever list is nonempty. Each node is visited once, giving O(n) time and O(1) extra space; this is optimal for the problem.
